comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–2027 Philosophy study guide and current programme page establish a 180-EC, three-year Dutch-language bachelor. Year 1 consists of eight compulsory 7.5-EC courses (60 EC). Year 2 consists of eight compulsory 7-EC courses plus Career Orientation (1 EC), Outside the Walls (2 EC), and Oral Philosophical Skills (1 EC), totalling 60 EC. Year 3 consists of a 30-EC approved minor outside Philosophy, 20 EC of level-3 Philosophy electives, and the 10-EC bachelor thesis and thesis course. The four Philosophy electives are instantiated using the first four courses in the study guide’s published level-3 elective list—Hegel’s Conception of Spirit, Ancient Buddhist Philosophy, Life, Mind, the Universe, and Happiness, and Heidegger’s Being and Time—as an objective source-order tie-break fixed before considering UCR fit. This is an elective-set instantiation, not a formal route. The minor remains genuine approved profile space outside Philosophy. All 180 EC are accounted for without inventing content.

alternatives.label: Philosophy across history, society and mind
alternatives.concept: Builds the broadest available UCR philosophy pathway from ethics, mind, self, political philosophy, logic and persuasive reasoning, complemented by history, literature and cultural interpretation. It addresses Groningen’s cross-subdisciplinary core while remaining less philosophically specialised than the comparator.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines all five available UCR philosophy courses with political philosophy, logic, rhetoric, historical context and interpretive humanities, so its defining feature is breadth across philosophical history, society and mind.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029. Personal & Professional Development is in Year 1; all course offerings match the fixed cohort terms; none of the selected courses has an unmet formal prerequisite; and eight level-3 courses are concentrated in Years 2 and 3 after introductory philosophy, politics, rhetoric, history and interpretive work.

alternatives.label: Ethics, politics, justice and institutions
alternatives.concept: Concentrates philosophical ethics and political thought around human rights, law, political institutions, social theory, conflict and public argument. It turns Groningen’s Ethics and Social and Political Philosophy directions into a materially different UCR curriculum rather than merely relabelling the broad closest match.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme is dominated by ethics and political philosophy, human-rights and public-law study, political institutions, social theory, conflict and argumentative communication; the label names those sustained priorities rather than the external package alone.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ten courses in archaeology, literary interpretation, intercultural history and general rhetoric with Law, Society & Justice, comparative politics, criminal and constitutional law, EU law, modern and contemporary sociology, environmental justice, gender history and an advanced history research seminar. The result prioritises normative public questions and institutions rather than a broad historical-philosophical survey.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Law, Society & Justice is completed in the first semester before Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Comparative Constitutional Law and Foundations of European Union Law. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and eight level-3 courses occur after introductory philosophy, politics, law and sociology.

alternatives.label: Mind, language, cognition and artificial intelligence
alternatives.concept: Develops Groningen’s Theoretical Philosophy direction through philosophy of mind, emotion, self and ethics, supported by logic, psycholinguistics, cognitive science, meaning, machine learning and AI ethics. The route studies representation and agency across philosophical, psychological and computational perspectives.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum clusters philosophy of mind, emotion and self with psycholinguistics, cognition, brain and behaviour, logic, meaning, machine learning and AI ethics; the final label states that interdisciplinary centre of gravity explicitly.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in political philosophy, law, history, archaeology, world literature and international politics with brain and behaviour, neurobiology, perception and action, psycholinguistics, social and experimental psychology, higher cognition, programming, machine learning, AI ethics and an advanced psychology research seminar. It therefore changes both the disciplinary mix and the central questions from broad philosophical history to mind, meaning and intelligent systems.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Introduction to Brain & Behavior is completed in semester 1 before Perception & Action, Psycholinguistics, Higher Order Functions and Advanced Research Seminar; introductory philosophy, rhetoric and brain science precede advanced mind, language and research work. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and seven level-3 courses occur in Years 2 and 3.

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the broad cross-subdisciplinary Philosophy core. The official Theoretical Philosophy direction and the combined Ethics and Social and Political Philosophy directions each produce coherent and materially distinct 24-course UCR curricula and are included as alternatives 3 and 2 respectively. The remaining official History of Philosophy direction is independently coherent, but the production contract permits at most three UCR alternatives; it is therefore recorded as maximum-reached rather than mischaracterised as incoherent or infeasible.

notes.text: Groningen provides a continuous 150-EC Philosophy curriculum around history of philosophy, theoretical and practical subdisciplines, advanced Philosophy electives and a required 10-EC thesis, alongside a 30-EC outside minor. UCR offers five dedicated Philosophy courses and builds related routes with Politics, Law, Communication, History, Literature, Sociology, Cognitive Science, Psychology and AI. Those interdisciplinary combinations are defensible pathways but do not reproduce Groningen’s sustained specialist Philosophy depth, its two-year compulsory sequence, four selected level-3 Philosophy electives, or its required Philosophy thesis.
